provenance.source: Personskatteloven; Aftale om reform af personskat (2025); PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Denmark; Danish payroll summaries of the 2026 rates
provenance.notes: AM-bidrag 8%, bundskat 12.01% and the average municipal rate of 25.049% came from PwC. The 2026 personal tax reform introduced a mellemskat and a top-topskat, whose thresholds came from Danish payroll summaries. The two sources disagreed on the top tax threshold, and the reform figures were used.

verificationTodo: SOURCES CONFLICT. PwC gives a single top tax of 7.5% above DKK 845,543; the reform summaries give mellemskat 7.5% above 641,200, topskat 7.5% above 777,900 and top-topskat 5% above 2,592,700. The reform figures are used here and must be confirmed with Skattestyrelsen.
The employment allowance maximum was reported as both DKK 56,200 and DKK 63,300. The higher figure is used here.
Confirm the personfradrag of DKK 54,100 for 2026.
omissions: The tax ceiling (skatteloft) capping the marginal rate at 60.5% including AM-bidrag is not applied.
Church tax, paid by members at roughly 0.7%, is not modelled.
The jobfradrag, the extra employment allowance for single parents and the pension contribution deduction are not modelled.

amBidrag.note: Charged first, on gross pay, before any allowance. Everything that follows is computed on the 92% that remains, which is why the headline rates understate the real burden.

employmentAllowance.note: A deduction from taxable income, raised to 12.75% by the 2026 reform. It reduces municipal tax but not bundskat.

personalAllowance.note: Deducted from the base of both bundskat and municipal tax.

stateTaxes.note: Bundskat is charged on personal income after the personal allowance. Mellemskat, topskat and top-topskat are charged on personal income above their thresholds, with no allowance.
